meta.title: Central Authorities Failed: A Father in Europe Could Not Have His Child Located or Returned | Bababou
meta.description: Summary of Central Authority failures in France, Norway and Germany: no location of the child, return refused or not registered, years of delays. A father’s experience under the Hague Convention.

hero.title: Central Authorities Failed: A Father in Europe Could Not Have His Child Located or Returned
hero.lead: Summary of institutional failures across three countries — no location of the child, return refused or not registered, years of delays.

summary.title: In short
summary.locatedBody: France, Norway and Germany did not locate the child; the father had to find her himself in Germany.
summary.norwayBody: Oslo District Court refused the petition for return under the Hague Convention (2016).
summary.germanyTitle: Germany refused to register the return request.
summary.germanyBody: The German Central Authority did not want to register the father’s request for return to France; the French authority initially said it was “not competent” for a displacement Norway→Germany.
summary.delayBody: Central Authorities took months or years to answer; procedures restarted when the child was moved to another country.

france.name: France
france.point1: Years of delay before meaningful action (e.g. contact with German authority only in 2026).
france.point2: Initially treated the case as “not competent” for displacement Norway→Germany; father had to insist on return to France.
france.point3: No location of the child by French authorities.

norway.name: Norway
norway.point1: Oslo District Court refused the petition for return (2016) on Convention grounds (habitual residence, Art. 3, 12, 13, 20).
norway.point2: No location of the child by Norwegian authorities; father had no effective remedy to have the child returned.

germany.name: Germany
germany.point1: Central Authority refused to register the return request (contradiction with visitation, Art. 12 delay, request to withdraw).
germany.point2: German authority “had no trace” of a 2022 return request; assumed return was to Norway, not France.
germany.point3: No location of the child by German authorities; father located the child himself in Frankfurt.
